h2: Marine NDT around Houston: barges, towboats, ship channel docks and offshore structures
html:
Marine NDT around Houston: barges, towboats, ship channel docks and offshore structures

Marine NDT in Houston mostly supports inland tank barges and towboats, ship channel docks and terminals, ships calling at Port Houston, and offshore platforms managed from the city. The work is mainly UT thickness gauging, MT on fatigue-prone details and close visual survey, done to a class society or Coast Guard requirement. Atlantis, a Houston company, sends crews to the vessel, dock or yard.

The inland fleet. Kirby Corporation is headquartered in Houston and is the largest liquid cargo barge operator in the US, with about 884 active inland tank barges and 251 towing vessels. Many other barge and towing companies operate on the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway as well. For NDT, that means a steady flow of shipyard periods. Bottom and side shell plating is gauged, cargo tanks are surveyed internally, and cracked or wasted structure is renewed and re-examined before the barge goes back to work.

Towing vessels under Subchapter M. Since 2016, US towing vessels 26 feet or longer, and smaller ones that move barges carrying oil or hazardous material in bulk, have come under 46 CFR Subchapter M. Owners can run a Towing Safety Management System audited by an approved third-party organization, or have the Coast Guard inspect directly. Either way, hull and machinery examinations need thickness data and records that the third-party organization or the Coast Guard inspector will accept. The gauging plan should be agreed with them before the vessel is hauled out.

Class work and approvals. ABS, a class society, has its world headquarters in Spring, just north of Houston. Its engineers and surveyors set many of the gauging plans that local crews work to. Class societies approve thickness measurement firms one by one. Whether Atlantis personnel are acceptable for a given class survey is confirmed with the surveyor at quotation, not assumed. The rules for that approval are explained on maritime NDT consulting in Houston.

Docks, terminals and offshore structures. Port Houston's complex of over 200 terminals, public and private, handles more foreign waterborne tonnage than any other US port. Their dock piping, loading-arm structures, crane pedestals and fender supports are checked by UT and MT while traffic keeps moving. Offshore platforms on the federal Outer Continental Shelf are regulated by the Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement under 30 CFR Part 250. Topside and splash-zone surveys there rely on UT, ACFM on coated nodes, and IRATA rope-access technicians where scaffolding is impractical.

  • Tank barges: bottom, side shell and cargo tank gauging during yard periods
  • Towboats: Subchapter M hull and machinery examination records
  • Ship channel docks: dock piping, loading-arm structures and crane pedestal welds
  • Offshore topsides: splash-zone UT and ACFM on nodes without stripping coatings
  • Hurricane season, June to November, which reshuffles yard and offshore schedules

Next steps. The national service is on maritime NDT services. Related Houston pages cover oil and gas NDT in Houston and every local service on inspection services in Houston. For in-house crews, see maritime NDT training. Gauging records can be kept and issued as signed reports in the Atlantis ERP reports app. Send vessel particulars and the survey requirement through the Houston marine NDT enquiry.
